review.headline: A wild tactical rollercoaster decided by early material gains

sections.text: Out of the Italian Game, your opponent handed you an immediate initiative with 7...b5. You seized it decisively with 8.Bxb5, setting up a pin against the knight on c6. After 8...a6, you followed up with 9.Bxc6+, executing a fork on the king and rook to win a piece and then the exchange with 10.Bxa8.

With a commanding material advantage, you continued expanding, later winning another rook with 17.Nxd8. However, complications arose when you pushed 21.d5, completely overlooking that your queen was under attack by the knight on c4. Black took your queen with 21...Nxd2, flipping the game in their favor.

Fortune swung right back when Black failed to capture your rook and played 22...f6. Even after another slip with 24.Nb1, Black returned the favor with 24...Qxe4. You consolidated with 25.Rxd2, kept your rooks active, and controlled the board until Black ran out of time on move 40.

review.turning_point: Black's early blunder 7...b5 allowed your decisive strike 8.Bxb5, giving you a winning material lead that survived late-game chaos.
review.focus: Always check for basic undefended pieces and direct threats before pushing pawns, as seen on 21.d5 where your queen was left hanging.

review.headline: A sharp central clash quickly unraveled on the kingside

sections.text: You stepped into a solid Petrov's Defense, but the game quickly grew complex once White pushed forward with 6.h4 and 7.d4. When White struck with 8.d5, opting for 8...hxg5 ran you into trouble. Instead, 8...Bg4 would have pinned the knight on f3 to the queen and kept your position sturdy. After 9.dxe6 fxe6 10.Nxg5, White gained dangerous central pressure against your weakened pawns.

The decisive moment arrived on move 10. You tried 10...Nd5, unleashing a discovered attack from your bishop on e7 against White's knight on g5. However, this left your key central squares undefended. White bypassed the threat immediately with 11.Nxe6, attacking your queen and completely shattering your defense.

After 13.Nxg7+ Kd8, your king was forced to run without castling rights. White offered a brief respite with 14.Bb5, but after 14...c6 15.Ne6+ Ke8 16.Ba4, you sought counterplay with 16...Nb6, creating a discovered attack from your queen on the e6-knight. White simply retreated with 17.Bb3 and broke open the center with 19.exd5, leaving your exposed king with no safe shelter.

review.turning_point: 10...Nd5 allowed White to land the devastating 11.Nxe6, winning critical material and dismantling your king's pawn cover beyond repair.
review.focus: Calculate your opponent's forcing replies before playing tactical shots like 10...Nd5, especially when your king remains uncastled in the center.
